title: Research: coalesce equivalent action proposals from independent local consumers before side effects
body:
## Purpose

Current-main intake: `cf07592b34cf3581d77f7cfda3855fa1e20e4255`.

#24 already covers retry/idempotency when the same semantic work is resubmitted after delivery uncertainty. #732 covers resource ownership/conflicts for resident local execution. This Issue isolates a different concurrency failure:

> Two independent local consumers may legitimately derive the same side-effecting proposal from the same world/intent state. Can the runtime coalesce those proposals into one semantic effect without suppressing a later action that only looks similar but belongs to a new state/effect opportunity?

This is not transport deduplication and not a new authority source.

## Example

```text
consumer A -> CLICK current Save
consumer B -> CLICK current Save
consumer C -> CLICK current Save
```

If all three mean the same current logical effect, executing all three may duplicate a side effect.

But:

```text
CLICK Next -> state changes -> CLICK Next
```

may be a valid repeated operation and must not be suppressed merely because coordinates/action type match.

## Candidate semantic identity

Do not freeze the exact schema by this Issue body, but the experiment must distinguish at least:
- intent/strategy revision;
- source observation/state generation;
- target identity/incarnation, not coordinate alone;
- operation/effect class;
- effect opportunity or expected postcondition;
- producer/proposal identity;
- expiry/deadline.

A proposal identity is evidence for coalescing; it is never authority.

## H — falsifiable hypothesis

Under one bounded concurrent-local task, effect-semantic coalescing can reduce duplicate effects from independently generated equivalent proposals to zero while preserving every preregistered legitimate repeated effect after the relevant state/effect generation changes.

## T — smallest discriminator

Authority-neutral/state-machine first.

Freeze a finite matrix including:

1. same state, same intent, same target/effect, two producers -> one effect;
2. same coordinates but different target incarnation -> not equivalent;
3. same target but different intent revision -> not automatically equivalent;
4. same operation after verified state transition -> legitimate second effect;
5. late equivalent proposal after first effect already satisfied -> NO_ACTION/SUPERSEDED;
6. same producer retry -> defer to #24 semantics rather than invent a second retry rule;
7. same semantic effect with altered parameters -> reject or treat distinct according to frozen effect contract;
8. ambiguous/missing effect identity -> YIELD/no coalescing claim.

Compare:
- `NO_CROSS_PRODUCER_COALESCING`
- `SEMANTIC_EFFECT_COALESCING`

Use a separately implemented oracle for expected effect cardinality.

### Live rung

Only after state-machine PASS. Use one controlled GUI operation with an independent application-effect scorer and two independent proposal producers. Each proposal must still pass ordinary current admission. Coalescing cannot turn an otherwise invalid proposal into valid input.

## D — decision

`PASS_CROSS_PRODUCER_EFFECT_COALESCING_SCOPED` requires:
- duplicate logical effects = 0 in all frozen equivalent-proposal cases;
- every legitimate repeated post-transition effect preserved;
- wrong-target/cross-intent/cross-incarnation merges = 0;
- unknown/ambiguous equivalence never guesses;
- no authority created or extended by coalescing state;
- release/cleanup remains correct;
- independent oracle/audit passes.

Failure dispositions:
- `FAIL_FALSE_COALESCE_VALID_REPEAT`
- `FAIL_DUPLICATE_EFFECT_REMAINS`
- `FAIL_CROSS_INTENT_OR_TARGET_MERGE`
- `HOLD_EXISTING_IDEMPOTENCY_ALREADY_SUFFICIENT`
- typed STOP for provenance/infrastructure.

## C — competing explanations

- #24 status/idempotency may already solve every real case once proposals reach a common semantic intent identity.
- A single-writer scheduler may avoid duplicates without semantic coalescing if only one proposal can be admitted per state generation.
- Effect identity may be impossible to know before application feedback; conservative YIELD may be required.
- Over-broad coalescing can silently lose legitimate repeated actions.

## U — limits

No exactly-once guarantee for arbitrary GUIs, distributed transaction claim, rollback guarantee or universal effect key follows from a scoped result.

## First stop

Run the finite authority-neutral matrix first. If ordinary #24 identity plus existing state-generation admission already distinguishes every case, close as redundant rather than adding another runtime abstraction.
